meta.name: Microsoft Security, Compliance & Identity Fundamentals (SC-900)
meta.notes: [bulk-tag pass: added `sc-900` tag to 60 questions] [sc-900 batch 1: 8 balanced rewrites]

questions.question: Which Zero Trust principle states that access should be granted based only on what a user needs to complete their current task, without granting broader permissions?
options: Assume breach
Use least privileg
Defense in depth
Verify explicitly
questions.explanation: Zero Trust's 'Use least privilege access' principle limits user rights with Just-In-Time and Just-Enough-Access (JIT/JEA), risk-based adaptive policies, and data protection. Users get only the permissions they need — nothing more. 'Verify explicitly' means always authenticate using all available signals. 'Assume breach' means design as if a breach has already occurred.

questions.question: A security team wants to design a network so that a compromised web server cannot directly access the internal database servers. Which security concept does this architecture implement?
options: Defense in depth
Single sign-on — restricting lateral movement
Zero Trust — assume breach
Conditional Access — network-based policy enforcement
questions.explanation: Defense in depth uses multiple security layers (network segmentation, firewalls, identity controls, encryption) so that a breach of one layer does not compromise the entire environment. Placing the database in an isolated network segment behind the web tier is a classic defense-in-depth network architecture.

questions.question: An employee receives an email that appears to be from IT support asking them to click a link and reset their password. This is an example of which type of attack?
options: Brute-force attack
SQL injection attack
Phishing attack
Man-in-the-middle attack
questions.explanation: Phishing is a social engineering attack that uses deceptive emails, messages, or websites to trick users into revealing credentials or clicking malicious links. Spear phishing is a targeted variant. Brute-force attacks guess passwords. Man-in-the-middle attacks intercept network traffic. SQL injection exploits database queries.

questions.question: The CIA triad is a foundational security model. An organisation encrypts customer data stored in its database. Which property of the CIA triad does this PRIMARILY protect?
options: Availability — ensuring authorised users can access data
Authentication — verifying the identity of users accessing data
Confidentiality
Integrity — ensuring data is accurate and unmodified
questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures that data is not exposed to unauthorised parties. Encryption is the primary technical control for confidentiality — even if an attacker accesses the storage medium, they cannot read the encrypted data without the key. Integrity protects against unauthorised modification. Availability ensures systems are accessible when needed.

questions.question: Under the Microsoft cloud shared responsibility model, when a company uses Azure SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365, which layer remains ALWAYS the customer's responsibility?
options: Network controls within the Azure backbone
Physical datacenter security
Operating system patching
Identity and access management for
questions.explanation: Regardless of the service model (IaaS, PaaS, or SaaS), customers retain responsibility for their own data, devices, and identity/access management. Microsoft manages the physical infrastructure, hypervisor, OS, and application stack for SaaS, but the customer must manage who has accounts, what roles they hold, and how they authenticate.

questions.question: Which Zero Trust guiding principle recommends treating every access request as if it originates from an untrusted network, even requests from inside the corporate perimeter?
options: Verify explicitly
Network segmentation
Assume breach
Use least privilege access
questions.explanation: 'Verify explicitly' means authenticate and authorise every request based on all available data points: identity, location, device health, service/workload, data classification, and anomalies. Never assume a request is trustworthy because it comes from inside the network — the traditional 'castle-and-moat' model is abandoned in Zero Trust.

questions.question: A hacker intercepts encrypted communications between a user and a banking website by positioning themselves between the two parties. This is BEST described as which type of attack?
options: Man-in-the-middle
Denial of Service (DoS)
Phishing
Password spray
questions.explanation: In a man-in-the-middle attack, the attacker secretly intercepts and potentially alters communications between two parties who believe they are communicating directly. Countermeasures include certificate pinning, HSTS, and mutual TLS. Password spray tries common passwords against many accounts. DoS floods a service to make it unavailable.

questions.question: Encryption in transit and encryption at rest are both used to protect data. Which scenario describes encryption IN TRANSIT?
options: A database stores customer records encrypted with AES-256
Data sent between a browser and a web server is protected using TLS
A BitLocker-encrypted laptop drive cannot be read if the laptop is stolen
A backup file on Azure Blob Storage uses server-side encryption
questions.explanation: Encryption in transit (also called encryption in motion) protects data as it moves across a network. TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the standard protocol for encrypting web traffic. Encryption at rest protects stored data — database encryption, blob storage SSE, and BitLocker are all examples of encryption at rest.

questions.question: A multinational firm runs Microsoft 365, several SaaS apps, and a fleet of in-house web apps. They want a single cloud identity-and-access service that authenticates employees and partners across all of these, supports conditional access policies, and acts as the IdP for SAML and OIDC apps. Which service does this?
options: Microsoft Entra ID
Microsoft Intune — endpoint management product that enforces device compliance and pushes configuration profiles; not an identity provider
Microsoft Sentinel — cloud-native SIEM that collects and correlates security telemetry across the estate; consumes identity events but does not issue them
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps — cloud access security broker that monitors SaaS usage and enforces session policies; not an identity store
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) is Microsoft's cloud-native identity platform. It provides authentication (sign-in), authorisation (access control), SSO, MFA, Conditional Access, and B2B/B2C collaboration. It is distinct from on-premises Windows Server Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS), although they can be synchronised.

questions.question: A user forgets their password and resets it themselves through a web portal without calling the help desk. Which Microsoft Entra ID feature enables this?
options: Multi-factor authentication (MFA); MFA adds a second factor to verify identity but does not allow a user to self-service reset their own password
Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
Conditional Access
Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR)
questions.explanation: Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) allows users to reset or unlock their own password without IT involvement, using verification methods such as an authenticator app, email, phone call, or security questions. SSPR reduces help desk calls and improves user productivity. It is configurable in the Microsoft Entra ID portal.

questions.question: An organisation wants to require all employees to verify their identity using a secondary method (e.g., a phone notification) in addition to their password when signing in. Which feature should they enable?
options: Multi-Factor Authenticat
Password Hash Synchronisation
Seamless SSO
Single Sign-On (SSO)
questions.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires two or more verification factors: something you know (password), something you have (phone/authenticator app), or something you are (biometric). Microsoft Entra MFA dramatically reduces the risk of account compromise from stolen passwords, as the attacker also needs the second factor.

questions.question: A company wants to allow employees to sign in to multiple SaaS applications (Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zoom) using a single set of corporate credentials, without re-entering passwords for each app. Which capability does this?
options: Identity Protection; Identity Protection evaluates sign-in risk signals but does not provide single sign-on capability to let users authenticate once for multiple apps
Multi-Factor Authentication
Conditional Access
Single Sign-On (SSO)
questions.explanation: Single Sign-On (SSO) lets users authenticate once with their corporate identity (Entra ID) and then access multiple applications without re-entering credentials. Microsoft Entra ID supports SSO via SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect, and OAuth 2.0. This improves user experience and reduces password fatigue.

questions.question: An administrator wants to block sign-ins from countries where the company has no employees, and require MFA for all admin roles. Which Microsoft Entra feature enforces these policies based on user and sign-in conditions?
options: Conditional Access policies
Identity Protection risk detections
Microsoft Entra ID Free tier tenant policies
Privileged Identity Management eligibility rules
questions.explanation: Conditional Access evaluates signals (user identity, group membership, device compliance, location, app, risk level) and enforces access decisions: allow, block, or require MFA/compliant device. It acts as an if-then policy engine. Blocking sign-ins from specific countries (named locations) and requiring MFA for admins are classic Conditional Access use cases.

questions.question: A developer deploys an Azure web application that needs to access Azure Key Vault to retrieve secrets. The developer does not want to store any credentials in the application code. Which identity type enables this?
options: A Managed Identity assigned to the Azure resource
A guest user account in Microsoft Entra ID; a guest user account is a human B2B identity in Entra ID and cannot be assigned as an azure managed identity for an azure resource
A service principal with a client secret stored in app settings
A shared access signature (SAS) token hardcoded in the application
questions.explanation: A Managed Identity provides an Azure resource (VM, App Service, Function App) with an automatically managed identity in Entra ID. The resource authenticates to Azure services like Key Vault using this identity — no secrets, passwords, or connection strings need to be stored in code or configuration. Azure manages the credential lifecycle.

questions.question: A company wants partner organisations to access its SharePoint intranet using their own corporate credentials, without creating separate accounts. Which Microsoft Entra capability supports this?
options: Microsoft Entra domain services for hybrid authentication
Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration.
Microsoft Entra B2C — for consumer-facing applications
Federation with on-premises Active Directory via ADFS
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra B2B (Business-to-Business) collaboration allows you to invite external users (from partner organisations) to access your resources. The guest users authenticate with their own organisational account or social identity — you don't manage their credentials. B2C is for customer-facing apps where consumers register their own accounts. inviting external users with their own identity

questions.question: Which Microsoft Entra ID feature detects risky sign-in behaviours such as sign-ins from anonymous IP addresses, impossible travel, and leaked credentials — and can automatically block or require MFA for those sessions?
options: Conditional Access named locations; Conditional Access named locations restrict access by geography but do not detect entra risk signals like impossible travel or leaked credentials
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Privileged Identity Management risk policies
Microsoft Sentinel — identity analytics
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID Protection uses machine learning to detect identity risk signals (anonymous IP, impossible travel, malware-linked IPs, leaked credentials, unfamiliar sign-in properties). It generates risk detections and risk levels (low, medium, high) that Conditional Access policies can act on — for example, requiring MFA for medium-risk sign-ins or blocking high-risk ones.

questions.question: A company wants to ensure that Global Administrators only have elevated privileges when actively performing admin tasks, not permanently. Admins should request and justify access before it is granted. Which feature achieves this?
options: Microsoft Entra Access Reviews
Self-Service Password Reset for admin accounts
Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Conditional Access with an admin-only named location
questions.explanation: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) provides Just-In-Time privileged access. Instead of permanently assigned admin roles, PIM makes users 'eligible' for roles. They must explicitly activate the role (provide a justification, get approved, use MFA) and the role expires after a configured time. This dramatically reduces standing privileged access exposure.

questions.question: An organisation uses both Microsoft Entra ID and on-premises Windows Server Active Directory. Which tool synchronises identities between on-premises AD and Entra ID so users can sign in to cloud apps with their corporate credentials?
options: Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS)
Microsoft Entra Connect (formerly Azure
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Microsoft Entra External ID
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Connect synchronises user accounts, groups, and password hashes (or hashes of hashes) from on-premises Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID. This enables hybrid identity — users get a single identity that works for both on-premises and cloud resources. It supports Password Hash Sync, Pass-Through Authentication, and Federation.

questions.question: A security administrator wants to review whether users still need their current group memberships and application access assignments, removing access that is no longer required. Which Microsoft Entra feature automates this process?
options: Microsoft Entra Access Reviews

Conditional Access — access control policies; Conditional Access enforces access policies but does not let an administrator review and certify whether current microsoft entra group memberships are still needed

Privileged Identity Management — eligibility reviews; Privileged Identity Management provides entra role eligibility but does not review whether microsoft 365 group or app access assignments are still justified
Identity Protection — risk remediation
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Access Reviews allow administrators (or resource owners) to periodically review and certify user access to groups, applications, and privileged roles. Reviewers confirm or remove assignments. Access Reviews can be scheduled to run automatically, reducing access sprawl and helping meet compliance requirements.

questions.question: A Microsoft Entra ID user is assigned the role 'Security Reader'. This role allows viewing security information in the Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Entra portals. Which type of role is this?
options: An Azure RBAC role scoped to a specific resource group; an Azure RBAC role is scoped to a specific azure resource group and does not grant permissions within microsoft entra directory services or the entra ID portal
A privileged role that requires activation through PIM
A Microsoft Entra built-in role that grants permissions within
A custom role created for a specific Conditional Access policy
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID has built-in roles (Global Administrator, Security Reader, User Administrator, etc.) that grant permissions across Entra ID and Microsoft 365 services. These are distinct from Azure RBAC roles, which control access to Azure resources (VMs, storage accounts, etc.). A user can hold Entra ID roles independently of any Azure resource permissions.

questions.question: Windows Hello for Business and FIDO2 security keys are both examples of which authentication approach in Microsoft Entra ID?
options: Federated authentication via SAML assertions
Multi-factor authentication using software tokens
Legacy authentication using basic authentication protocols
Passwordless authentication.
questions.explanation: Passwordless authentication eliminates passwords entirely. Microsoft Entra supports three main passwordless methods: Windows Hello for Business (biometric/PIN tied to device), FIDO2 security keys (hardware tokens like YubiKey), and the Microsoft Authenticator app (fingerprint/face + phone possession). These are more secure than passwords because there are no passwords to steal or guess. verifying identity without a password

questions.question: A company builds a consumer-facing mobile app where customers can sign up with their email, Google, or Facebook accounts. Which Microsoft Entra capability is designed for this use case?
options: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
Entra ID free tier with social identity provider federation
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Microsoft Entra External ID — B2C
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra External ID for customers (B2C) is specifically designed for consumer-facing applications. It allows customers to register and sign in with their own email address or social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple) and provides customisable sign-up/sign-in user flows. B2B is for partner/employee collaboration, not consumer apps.

questions.question: A platform team wants a single console that continuously assesses their Azure and AWS workloads against best-practice benchmarks, surfaces risky misconfigurations, and also raises runtime threat alerts when workloads behave abnormally. They want both posture and workload protection from one service. Which service delivers this?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Sentinel — cloud-native SIEM/SOAR that collects logs and runs detections; does not perform native posture benchmarking against cloud control planes
Microsoft Purview — governance and compliance suite focused on data classification, lineage, and DLP; not a workload-protection tool
Microsoft Intune — device management for endpoints; outside the cloud-workload protection domain entirely
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud serves two main functions: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) — continuously assessing the security configuration of your cloud resources and providing a Secure Score — and Cloud Workload Protection (CWP) — detecting and responding to threats on Azure VMs, containers, databases, and even multi-cloud workloads (AWS, GCP). It is not a SIEM (that's Microsoft Sentinel) or an EDR (that's Defender for Endpoint). AWS, and GCP

questions.question: A security team receives a Secure Score of 42% in Microsoft Defender for Cloud. What does this score represent?
options: The organisation has implemented 42% of the recommended security controls to
The organisation's compliance with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework is 42%
42% of security incidents have been resolved in the current month
42% of company devices have Defender antivirus enabled
questions.explanation: Secure Score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud measures how well your current security configuration implements recommended security controls. A higher score means more recommendations have been applied. Defender for Cloud provides prioritised recommendations and the expected score improvement for each, helping teams focus on the most impactful security improvements.

questions.question: Which Microsoft service is a cloud-native Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) solution?
options: Microsoft Sentinel
Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Defender XDR
Microsoft Purview Audit
questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native SIEM (collects and analyses security data from across the environment) and SOAR (automates responses using playbooks powered by Azure Logic Apps). It ingests data from Microsoft and non-Microsoft sources, uses built-in analytics rules to detect threats, and can automatically trigger remediation actions.

questions.question: A security team configures Microsoft Sentinel to automatically isolate a compromised device when a high-severity alert fires, without manual intervention. Which Sentinel feature enables this automated response?
options: Hunting queries — proactive threat searches; hunting queries in Sentinel are proactive manual searches, not automated workflows triggered by incoming alerts
Workbooks — visualises security data in dashboards
Playbooks — automated workflows triggered by alerts
Analytics rules — detects threats by querying logs
questions.explanation: Sentinel Playbooks are automated workflows built on Azure Logic Apps that run in response to alerts or incidents. They can perform actions like sending notifications, isolating endpoints, blocking IP addresses, or creating tickets — without human intervention. This is the SOAR capability of Sentinel. Analytics rules detect threats; workbooks visualise data; hunting is proactive investigation.

questions.question: Which Microsoft Defender solution is specifically designed to detect and respond to threats on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android endpoints — providing endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities?
options: Microsoft Defender for Identity; Microsoft Defender for Identity monitors Active Directory signals and does not protect endpoint operating systems with detection and response capabilities
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint is an enterprise EDR platform that provides attack surface reduction, next-generation protection, endpoint detection and response, automated investigation and remediation, and vulnerability management across all major device operating systems. Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB. Defender for Identity protects Active Directory. Defender for Office 365 secures email.

questions.question: An organisation uses Microsoft 365. Which solution protects users against malicious links in emails (Safe Links), unknown malware in attachments (Safe Attachments), and anti-phishing policies?
options: Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Microsoft Purview Information Protection
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (Plan 1 and Plan 2) adds advanced threat protection to Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, and OneDrive. Key features include Safe Links (rewrites URLs to check them at click time), Safe Attachments (detonates suspicious files in a sandbox), anti-phishing with impersonation protection, and attack simulation training.

questions.question: A company uses many SaaS applications (Salesforce, Dropbox, Zoom). The security team wants visibility into which applications are being used, by whom, and the ability to block access to unapproved apps. Which service provides this Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) capability?
options: Microsoft Sentinel data connectors; Sentinel data connectors ingest logs into the SIEM but cannot discover shadow IT apps or block access to unapproved cloud apps in a CASB role
Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps (formerly Microsoft Cloud App Security) is Microsoft's CASB. It provides shadow IT discovery (what apps are being used), data protection (DLP for cloud apps), threat protection, and compliance assessment. It can block access to non-sanctioned apps by integrating with Conditional Access or a network proxy.

questions.question: Which Microsoft Defender solution monitors on-premises Active Directory signals to detect attacks such as pass-the-hash, pass-the-ticket, and Kerberos brute-force attacks against domain controllers?
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Defender for Identity
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity (formerly Azure Advanced Threat Protection / ATP) monitors on-premises Active Directory Domain Services. It analyses network traffic to domain controllers and Windows events to detect identity-based attacks: pass-the-hash, pass-the-ticket, Kerberoasting, Golden/Silver ticket attacks, reconnaissance, and lateral movement. Entra ID Protection focuses on cloud sign-in risk.

questions.question: The Microsoft Defender portal (security.microsoft.com) consolidates alerts and incidents from multiple Defender products into a unified view. This unified extended detection and response platform is known as what?
options: Microsoft Purview Compliance Portal
Microsoft Defender for Cloud
Microsoft Defender XDR
Microsoft Sentinel
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender XDR (Extended Detection and Response) is the integrated security platform that brings together Defender for Endpoint, Defender for Office 365, Defender for Identity, and Defender for Cloud Apps into a single pane of glass at security.microsoft.com. It correlates signals across all these products into unified incidents, enabling faster detection and coordinated response.

questions.question: An organisation wants to protect its web applications running on Azure App Service from OWASP Top 10 threats like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS). Which Azure service should be deployed?
options: Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on
Azure DDoS Protection Standard
Microsoft Defender for App Service
Azure Network Security Groups (NSGs)
questions.explanation: Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) is a managed rule set that inspects HTTP/HTTPS traffic for OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQL injection, XSS, remote file inclusion, etc.). It can be deployed on Azure Application Gateway, Azure Front Door, or Azure CDN. NSGs operate at the network layer (IP/port) and cannot inspect application-layer attacks. DDoS Protection defends against volumetric attacks.

questions.question: A company is concerned about large-scale volumetric network attacks (UDP floods, ICMP floods) targeting its Azure public IP addresses. Which service provides dedicated protection against these distributed denial-of-service attacks?
options: Azure Web Application Firewall — inspects layer-7 traffic for attack patterns; the WAF inspects layer-7 HTTP traffic for OWASP threats but does not provide protection against volumetric UDP or ICMP DDoS floods
Azure Firewall — blocks malicious traffic by IP and FQDN
Network Security Groups — filters traffic using port and protocol rules
Azure DDoS Protection
questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection Standard provides always-on traffic monitoring and automatic mitigation of DDoS attacks targeting Azure public IP addresses. It defends against volumetric attacks (UDP floods, amplification attacks), protocol attacks (SYN floods), and resource-layer attacks. There is a Basic tier included free with Azure, and Standard (now called Network Protection) provides enhanced mitigation, alerting, and telemetry.

questions.question: An Azure architect is choosing between two L3/L4 controls. The first is a stateful, regional, managed firewall product with its own public IP, threat-intel feed, and FQDN filtering. The second is a free, distributed packet filter attached to subnets or NICs. Which statement best describes the difference?
options: The first is a basic stateless ACL; the second is a fully managed firewall service with a public IP and threat-intelligence integration for outbound rules; NSGs are stateless packet-level ACLs that filter by IP and port and cannot perform stateful inspection, threat-intel feeds, or fqdn-based filtering of outbound traffic
The first is a stateful, fully managed network firewall (own public IP, threat-intel, FQDN filtering)
Both are identical Azure resources marketed under different names depending on whether the subscription has Defender for Cloud enabled
The first runs only on Azure Stack Edge for on-prem deployments; the second is exclusive to Azure regions in the cloud
questions.explanation: Azure Firewall is a managed, cloud-native firewall with stateful packet inspection, FQDN filtering, threat intelligence integration, and centralised policy management. It operates at a higher level and can control traffic across the entire VNet or multiple VNets. NSGs are lighter-weight, network-layer access control lists (ACLs) applied to subnets or NICs — they filter by source/destination IP, port, and protocol, but cannot do FQDN-based filtering. managed network firewall service that can filter traffic across subscriptions and VNets using FQDN rules; NSGs are simpler network-layer filters (IP/port) applied to subnets or NICs

questions.question: A company wants to store and control access to API keys, database connection strings, and TLS certificates used by its Azure applications. Which Azure service is designed for this purpose?
options: Microsoft Entra ID — storing app credentials as service principal secrets
Azure App Configuration — storing application settings and feature flags
Azure Blob Storage with encryption at rest
Azure Key Vault
questions.explanation: Azure Key Vault is the dedicated secrets management service. It stores secrets (API keys, connection strings, passwords), cryptographic keys (used for encryption/decryption), and certificates (TLS/SSL). Access is controlled via Key Vault access policies or Azure RBAC. Auditing is built in. Applications retrieve secrets via the SDK or REST API, keeping secrets out of code and config files. keys, and certificates

questions.question: An app developer stores a TLS private key and a database connection string in Azure Key Vault. The vault treats them differently: one is wrapped by an HSM and can be invoked for sign/encrypt operations without ever leaving the boundary, while the other is simply stored as an opaque string the app fetches at startup. Which statement describes the distinction?
options: Both are opaque byte strings; the only difference is the audit-log verbosity at which Key Vault records read operations; keys and secrets are not both opaque byte strings — keys are cryptographic material used to sign and encrypt without leaving the HSM boundary, whereas secrets are opaque stored strings the app retrieves
Keys are stored as cryptographic material protected by the HSM and used for sign/encrypt operations without leaving the boundary
Keys are restricted to symmetric AES; secrets must be used for any asymmetric RSA or EC material in the vault
Keys are billed per access, while secrets are billed per byte stored regardless of how often they are retrieved
questions.explanation: Keys in Key Vault are cryptographic keys (RSA, EC). Cryptographic operations (encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify) are performed BY Key Vault — the key material never leaves the vault. Secrets are arbitrary string values (passwords, API tokens, connection strings) that you store and later retrieve. Certificates are a third type, combining a public certificate and its associated private key.

questions.question: A security team wants to enable Just-In-Time (JIT) access to Azure virtual machines so that management ports (RDP/SSH) are not permanently open on the internet. Which service provides this?
options: Microsoft Entra PIM — activates admin roles for VM management
Azure Bastion — browser-based RDP/SSH without public internet exposure
Azure Firewall — blocks all inbound RDP connections by default
Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
questions.explanation: Just-In-Time VM access in Microsoft Defender for Cloud locks down inbound traffic to Azure VMs by creating a 'deny-all' NSG rule for management ports. When an admin requests access, Defender for Cloud temporarily opens the port for a specified time and source IP, then closes it again. Azure Bastion is also a good answer for secure VM access, but JIT is the specific feature described. JIT VM access feature that creates time-limited NSG rules on demand

questions.question: Which Microsoft Sentinel component connects Sentinel to external data sources — such as Microsoft Entra ID logs, Office 365 activity logs, and third-party firewalls — to ingest security data for analysis?
options: Playbooks
Workbooks
Data connecto
Analytics rules
questions.explanation: Data connectors in Microsoft Sentinel are the ingestion pipelines that bring log data from various sources into the Log Analytics workspace that Sentinel uses. Microsoft provides out-of-the-box connectors for Azure services, Microsoft 365, Microsoft Defender products, and many third-party sources (Palo Alto, Check Point, Cisco, Syslog, CEF). Without data connectors, Sentinel has no data to analyse.

questions.question: Microsoft Defender for Cloud markets two complementary capability categories. One focuses on detecting and reducing misconfigurations and improving the customer's security posture against benchmarks. The other adds runtime threat detection and protection for specific workload types (VMs, SQL, containers, storage). Which pair correctly names these categories?
options: Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM)

Identity and Access Management (IAM) and Mobile Device Management (MDM) — both focused on user and device administration; IAM and MDM manage identities and devices but are not the cloud security posture management pairing for assessing cloud workload misconfigurations
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Information Rights Management (IRM) — both focused on document and email protection
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) and Security Orchestration Automation and Response (SOAR) — both focused on log analytics and playbook execution
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud's two pillars are: (1) CSPM — assess security configurations, compute Secure Score, provide hardening recommendations, enforce Azure Security Benchmark; and (2) CWP (also called Defender Plans) — detect and respond to threats targeting specific workload types: servers, containers, databases, storage, Key Vault, App Service, and multi-cloud resources.

questions.question: A data-governance lead is shopping for a unified product that catalogues all data across SQL, blob storage, Power BI, and on-prem sources; classifies sensitive data; tracks lineage; applies labels; and exposes compliance and risk insights. Microsoft markets a single suite that does this. Which product is it?
options: Microsoft Purview
Microsoft Sentinel — cloud-native SIEM/SOAR that collects security telemetry and runs detections; not a data-governance catalogue
Microsoft Defender for Cloud — workload security posture and threat protection; not a governance catalogue
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management — cloud infrastructure entitlement management product, scoped to permissions rather than data
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview is the umbrella brand for Microsoft's data governance and compliance portfolio. It includes the Microsoft Purview compliance portal (for compliance management, data classification, DLP, retention, eDiscovery, audit) and data governance capabilities (cataloguing and understanding data across the organisation). It was formed by merging Azure Purview and the Microsoft 365 compliance centre.

questions.question: A compliance team wants to assess their organisation's compliance posture against regulations like GDPR, ISO 27001, and HIPAA, and track improvement over time. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this?
options: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery — searches and exports content for legal review; eDiscovery searches and exports content for legal review and does not score compliance posture or track improvement actions against regulatory frameworks
Microsoft Purview Audit — logs user and admin activities
Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager.
Microsoft Purview Information Protection — classifies sensitive data
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager in Microsoft Purview provides a centralised dashboard showing your compliance posture against multiple regulatory frameworks. It calculates a compliance score based on the controls you've implemented (or verified), maps Microsoft's responsibilities vs. your responsibilities, and provides recommended improvement actions with step-by-step guidance. provides assessments, a compliance score, and recommended actions

questions.question: A company's legal team needs to search all emails and Teams messages sent by a specific employee over the past 90 days in connection with a lawsuit, and place a hold so that content cannot be deleted. Which Microsoft Purview capability is used?
options: Retention policies — automatically retain or delete content on a schedule; retention policies automatically retain or delete content on a schedule and do not allow a legal team to search specific employee messages or place a litigation hold
eDiscovery — search, preserve, collect, review,.
Audit — logs who accessed or modified content
Communication compliance — reviews messages for policy violations
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery (Standard and Premium) supports legal hold, content search across Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, Viva Engage, and OneDrive, review sets, and export. Placing a hold prevents content from being deleted or modified. Premium eDiscovery adds advanced capabilities like AI-based document analysis and case management for large-scale investigations. and export content for legal proceedings

questions.question: A data protection officer wants to classify documents containing credit card numbers as 'Confidential – Financial' and automatically encrypt them when shared externally. Which Microsoft Purview feature applies classification and protection to documents and emails?
options: Sensitivity labels — classify and optionally apply protection (encryption,.

Compliance Manager controls — document security processes; Compliance Manager tracks control implementation and documents security processes but cannot classify documents or apply encryption protection to email or files
Retention labels — control how long content is kept
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies — detect and block sharing of sensitive data
questions.explanation: Sensitivity labels in Microsoft Purview Information Protection classify documents and emails with labels (Confidential, Public, Highly Confidential, etc.) and can apply protection: encryption (with rights like 'read only' or 'no copy'), content markings (headers, footers, watermarks), and access restrictions. Labels can be applied manually by users or automatically based on sensitive information type detections. watermarking, access restrictions) to content

questions.question: A security team wants to prevent employees from accidentally emailing documents containing patient health information (PHI) outside the organisation. Which Microsoft Purview feature detects and blocks this?
options: Insider risk management — detects anomalous user behaviour patterns
Sensitivity labels — the employee's label choice controls sharing
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies.
Communication compliance — reviews messages for inappropriate content
questions.explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies in Microsoft Purview automatically inspect content in Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and endpoints for sensitive information types (credit card numbers, SSNs, health record identifiers, etc.). When a violation is detected, DLP can block the action, show a policy tip to the user, and log the event. This is the right tool for preventing accidental or deliberate exfiltration of sensitive data. scan content for sensitive information types and block/warn/audit when policy is violated

questions.question: A regulated company must retain all emails for 7 years for legal and audit purposes, and automatically delete them after 10 years. Which Microsoft Purview feature automates this content lifecycle?
options: Communication compliance — log all messages for compliance review
Sensitivity labels with auto-apply encryption rules
Retention policies or retention labels.
eDiscovery holds — keep specific content for indefinite periods
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview retention policies and labels govern the data lifecycle. Retention policies apply to entire locations (all Exchange mailboxes, all SharePoint sites). Retention labels provide item-level control. Both let you define a retention period (7 years) and a disposition action (delete or review when expired). This satisfies regulatory requirements for records management. define how long content is retained and what happens after the period expires

questions.question: A company wants to detect if employees are leaking intellectual property by copying files to USB drives or uploading to personal cloud storage. Which Microsoft Purview solution is designed for this use case?
options: Communication compliance — reviews messages for sensitive content
Data Loss Prevention (DLP) — blocks exfiltration of classified files
eDiscovery — searches for specific files matching evidence criteria
Insider Risk Management
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management detects anomalous user behaviour that may indicate insider threats: data theft by departing employees, sensitive data leaks, security policy violations, and more. It uses machine learning to analyse signals across Microsoft 365 (file downloads, Teams messages, browser activity with Endpoint DLP) and surfaces risk cases for investigation. DLP can block the action, but Insider Risk Management identifies the risky user pattern.

questions.question: Which Microsoft Purview feature provides an immutable log of user and admin activities (such as email read, file downloaded, admin role change) across Microsoft 365 services for security investigation and compliance reporting?
options: Microsoft Purview Audit
Microsoft Sentinel — audit log data connector; Microsoft Sentinel uses a purview audit log data connector to ingest activity records but is not the source of the immutable purview audit log itself
Microsoft Defender for Cloud activity log
Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview Audit (Standard and Premium) records user and admin activity across Exchange Online, SharePoint, Teams, OneDrive, and other Microsoft 365 services. Audit Standard retains logs for 180 days; Audit Premium extends this to 1 year (or 10 years with an add-on) and adds intelligent insights. Administrators can search the audit log for forensic investigation and compliance evidence.

questions.question: An organisation needs to ensure that employees in the legal department cannot communicate with employees in the trading desk to prevent conflicts of interest. Which Microsoft Purview feature enforces these communication restrictions?
options: Communication compliance — flags messages for review by compliance officers
Retention policies — control how long messages are stored
Data Loss Prevention — blocks email content matching financial keywords
Information barriers
questions.explanation: Information barriers in Microsoft Purview are policies that prevent specific segments of users from communicating with each other in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive. They are used in regulated industries (financial services, law firms, government) to prevent conflicts of interest, insider trading, and breaches of fiduciary duty. Unlike communication compliance (which reviews after-the-fact), information barriers block the communication from occurring.

questions.question: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance helps organisations detect messages in Teams, Exchange, and Viva Engage that may violate company policies. Which of the following is a typical use case?
options: Preventing users from downloading files from SharePoint to personal devices
Detecting and reviewing messages containing harassment.
Blocking emails containing credit card numbers from leaving the organisation
Automatically deleting Teams messages after 90 days
questions.explanation: Communication compliance uses machine learning classifiers and keyword policies to surface messages in Teams, Exchange, and Viva Engage that may contain harassment, threatening language, adult content, or regulatory violations (like sharing investment advice). A compliance reviewer examines flagged messages and takes action. It is a supervisory/review tool, not a blocking tool like DLP. inappropriate language, or regulatory violations (such as stock tip sharing)

questions.question: In Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager, an administrator opens a regulatory template and sees a single number summarising progress. The number reflects how many recommended actions — Microsoft-managed plus customer-managed — are completed, weighted by risk. What does the number measure?
options: The percentage of users who completed annual compliance training over the trailing 90-day window inside the tenant
Progress toward implementing recommended controls (improvement actions), weighted by risk and split between Microsoft-managed and

The exact financial penalty avoided by current control implementation under the active regulatory templates; financial penalty avoided is not what the compliance score measures — it tracks progress on microsoft-managed and customer-managed recommended improvement actions weighted by risk
Current count of active alerts and incidents in Defender for Cloud across the customer's subscriptions
questions.explanation: The compliance score in Compliance Manager measures progress on completing recommended improvement actions that are mapped to compliance framework controls (GDPR, ISO 27001, NIST, HIPAA, etc.). A higher score means more controls are in place. Microsoft's actions (things Microsoft does to maintain its cloud compliance) are pre-credited. You work on customer-managed actions to improve your score.

questions.question: A company is evaluating Azure Bastion for remote access to Azure VMs. Which statement BEST describes Azure Bastion's security benefit?
options: Azure Bastion allows RDP/SSH access through the browser using TLS.

Azure Bastion replaces the need for NSGs on VM subnets; Azure Bastion does not replace the need for NSGs because NSGs still restrict lateral network access between subnets and VMs within the virtual network
Azure Bastion encrypts all RDP/SSH traffic using AES-256
Azure Bastion provides MFA for all VM connections automatically
questions.explanation: Azure Bastion is a PaaS service that provides secure RDP/SSH access to Azure VMs directly from the Azure portal over TLS (port 443), without exposing the VMs to the internet. VMs do not need public IP addresses, and port 3389 (RDP) and 22 (SSH) do not need to be open on NSGs. This eliminates a common attack surface — internet-facing management ports. without requiring public IP addresses or open RDP/SSH ports on the VMs

questions.question: Which term describes the security model in which trust is never assumed by default, every access request is fully verified, and access is designed to minimise damage from potential breaches?
options: Perimeter security; perimeter security assumes internal traffic can be trusted without verification and is the model that zero trust explicitly rejects
Zero Trust
Defense in depth; defense in depth layers multiple security controls but does not specifically require verifying every access request regardless of trust level or network location
Shared responsibility
questions.explanation: Zero Trust is a security model based on three principles: (1) Verify explicitly — always authenticate and authorise based on all available data; (2) Use least privilege access — limit user rights with JIT/JEA; (3) Assume breach — minimise blast radius, segment access, verify end-to-end encryption, use analytics to detect anomalies. It replaces the old 'trust but verify' perimeter model.

questions.question: A developer registers a new application in Entra ID so the app can call Microsoft Graph using its own identity. Entra creates a directory object for that application's identity within the tenant. Roles and permissions are granted to this object so the app can sign in headlessly. What is this object?
options: A guest user — an external identity invited as a B2B collaborator, intended for human partners rather than automated workloads
A service principal
A managed group — a synced group used for Conditional Access scoping, not an authentication identity
A device object — the directory record of an enrolled endpoint, used to gate compliance and conditional access on hardware
questions.explanation: A service principal is an instance of an application's registration in a specific Entra ID tenant — it is the application's identity. When you register an app in Entra ID (creating an 'App registration'), a service principal is created in the tenant. The service principal can be granted permissions to Azure resources or Entra ID APIs. Managed identities are a special type of service principal managed automatically by Azure.

questions.question: A Microsoft Entra tenant has both 'Free' and 'P1' licensed users. Which feature is ONLY available with the P1 or P2 license?
options: Multi-Factor Authentication for global administrators
User account creation and management
Conditional Access policies
Basic security reports and audit logs
questions.explanation: Conditional Access policies require Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or P2) licensing. The free tier includes basic MFA for global admins (via Security Defaults), basic audit logs, and SSO for up to 10 apps. P1 unlocks Conditional Access (granular if-then access rules), advanced group management, and more. P2 adds Identity Protection, PIM, and Access Reviews.

questions.question: Which Microsoft Purview feature allows users to submit their personal data privacy requests (access, deletion) and helps organisations manage those requests in accordance with privacy regulations like GDPR?
options: Compliance Manager — GDPR assessment
Microsoft Purview Audit
Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Microsoft Priva
questions.explanation: Microsoft Priva (part of the Microsoft Purview family) provides two solutions: Privacy Risk Management (identifies privacy risks in data stored in Microsoft 365, such as data transfers or overexposed personal data) and Subject Rights Requests (automates the process of finding, reviewing, and responding to requests from individuals to access, correct, or delete their personal data under GDPR, CCPA, etc.).

questions.question: Microsoft Defender for Cloud shows a recommendation: 'Enable MFA for accounts with owner permissions on your subscription.' This recommendation appears in which Defender for Cloud pillar?
options: Defender plans — protects specific resource types
Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM).
Cloud Workload Protection — threat detection for running workloads
Regulatory compliance — maps controls to NIST framework requirements
questions.explanation: CSPM in Defender for Cloud continuously assesses the security configuration of your subscriptions and resources against the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark and other frameworks. Recommendations like 'Enable MFA for owners' are CSPM findings — they identify misconfigurations or security gaps in your posture. Implementing them improves your Secure Score. This is distinct from threat detection (CWP), which detects active attacks. identifies misconfigurations and security risks

questions.question: What type of attack does Azure DDoS Protection Standard NOT defend against, requiring Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) instead?
options: ICMP floods targeting public IP addresses; ICMP floods are volumetric layer-3 DDoS attacks that Azure DDoS Protection defends against — not application-layer HTTP attacks that require a WAF
SYN floods targeting TCP connections
HTTP/HTTPS application-layer attacks like HTTP
UDP amplification floods targeting DNS servers
questions.explanation: Azure DDoS Protection defends against volumetric attacks (UDP floods, DNS amplification), protocol attacks (SYN floods, reflection attacks), and state exhaustion attacks at layers 3 and 4. However, application-layer (layer 7) attacks — HTTP floods, slow HTTP attacks, API abuse — require a WAF to inspect and filter HTTP traffic. DDoS Protection and WAF are complementary defences.

questions.question: An organisation's Security Operations Centre (SOC) team uses Microsoft Sentinel. An analyst runs a KQL query to search through 30 days of logs looking for signs of suspicious activity that doesn't match existing alert rules. Which Sentinel capability describes this proactive activity?
options: Workbooks — visual dashboards for security data; workbooks display visual dashboards of security data and are not designed for proactive analyst-driven threat search using custom KQL queries
Analytics rules — scheduled queries that generate alerts automatically
Playbooks — automated response workflows
Hunting — proactive threat search using custom KQL queries
questions.explanation: Hunting in Microsoft Sentinel allows security analysts to proactively search for threats across their data using custom KQL (Kusto Query Language) queries. It is hypothesis-driven investigation — analysts look for indicators of compromise, abnormal behaviour, or attacker techniques (MITRE ATT&CK) that haven't triggered automated alerts. Hunting differs from analytics rules, which run automatically on a schedule.

questions.question: Which Microsoft security product provides mobile device management (MDM) and mobile application management (MAM) to ensure corporate devices and apps comply with security policies before accessing corporate resources?
options: Microsoft Intune
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps — CASB for SaaS applications
Microsoft Entra ID — device registration only
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint — EDR for managed devices
questions.explanation: Microsoft Intune (part of Microsoft Endpoint Manager / Microsoft Intune Suite) provides MDM (enrol and manage whole devices — configure settings, enforce encryption, wipe if lost) and MAM (wrap individual apps with policies without enrolling the entire device — useful for BYOD). Intune integrates with Conditional Access so only compliant devices can access corporate resources.

questions.question: A company needs to ensure that only devices that are registered with the company and meet compliance requirements (e.g., encrypted, patched, no jailbreak) can access Microsoft 365 email. Which combination of services enforces this?
options: Microsoft Intune (device compliance policies) and

Microsoft Purview DLP and retention policies; Purview DLP and retention policies govern data content lifecycle but cannot enforce device compliance or gate access to Microsoft 365 email based on device state
Azure DDoS Protection and Azure Firewall
Microsoft Defender for Cloud CSPM and Secure Score
questions.explanation: The standard pattern for device-based access control is: (1) Intune defines compliance policies (must be encrypted, PIN required, OS version minimum, etc.); (2) Devices that meet these policies are marked compliant in Entra ID; (3) Conditional Access policy requires a 'compliant device' grant condition for access to Exchange/Microsoft 365. Non-compliant or unregistered devices are blocked.
